#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Waits for the iPad to answer, then copies Manic's crash reports and session logs here.
set -u
. "$HOME/.local/share/ios-signer/scripts/env.sh"
OUT="$(dirname "$0")"
TOOL="$SIGNER_HOME/bin/rpcheck-logs"
BUNDLE="com.globocodes.manicemu"
deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 6*3600 ))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$deadline" ]; do
    host="$(signer_find_ipad 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$host" ]; then
        echo "$(date -Is) iPad answers on $host"
        "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" crashlogs ManicEmu > "$OUT/crashlogs.txt" 2> "$OUT/crashlogs.err" || { cat "$OUT/crashlogs.err"; }
        cat "$OUT/crashlogs.txt"
        grep -v '^pairing\|^tunnel' "$OUT/crashlogs.txt" | awk -F'\t' '$2=="S_IFREG"{print $1}' | tail -12 | while read -r name; do
            "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" crashpull "$name" "$OUT/$name" 2>&1 | tail -1
        done
        "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" docs-ls "$BUNDLE" "/Documents/Netplay Logs" > "$OUT/netplay-logs.txt" 2> "$OUT/netplay-logs.err" || { cat "$OUT/netplay-logs.err"; }
        cat "$OUT/netplay-logs.txt"
        "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" docs-pull "$BUNDLE" "/Documents/Netplay Logs/Manic MP sessions.log" "$OUT/Manic MP sessions.log" 2>&1 | tail -1
        grep -v '^pairing\|^tunnel' "$OUT/netplay-logs.txt" | awk -F'\t' '$2=="S_IFREG" && $1!="Manic MP sessions.log"{print $4"\t"$1}' | sort | tail -4 | cut -f2 | while read -r name; do
            "$TOOL" "$host" "$IPAD_PAIRING" docs-pull "$BUNDLE" "/Documents/Netplay Logs/$name" "$OUT/$name" 2>&1 | tail -1
        done
        echo "$(date -Is) pull finished"
        exit 0
    fi
    sleep 60
done
echo "$(date -Is) gave up: iPad never answered"
exit 3
EOF
chmod +x $S/ipad-pull/watch-and-pull.sh; echo written; $S/ipad-pull/watch-and-pull.sh

payload.text:
Root cause found from the iPad's own crash report, and the fix is in place awaiting your ship go-ahead.

**What crashed.** The Shrek 2 launch on Oct 16 at 23:42 died on Dolphin's CPU thread with a bus error. The kernel refused to execute the very first block of Dolphin's JIT code buffer as unsigned code. The report carries the sticky "has been debugged" flag, and the code region was mapped read-execute, so Manic believed JIT was fine.

**Why it only happens sometimes.** Your iPad is TXM-class hardware on iPadOS 26. There, JIT only works while StikDebug is actually attached, because the core asks the attached debugger to make each JIT region executable. StikDebug had attached at app launch at 23:36, then got suspended or killed in the background. The game started 6.5 minutes later. The fork's JIT check only looked at the sticky flag, which never clears after the debugger leaves, so Dolphin booted on JIT with nobody to grant it. A fresh app launch re-attaches StikDebug and works, which is what made it look random. The Animal Crossing session you started right after the crash ran fine for exactly that reason.

**The fix.**
- RetroArch fork, new branch `game-start-crash` (pushed, pin moved to it): on TXM hardware JIT availability now also requires a live tracer, read via the process flags. PPL devices keep the old behaviour. A new "JIT debugger detached" query is exposed to the app.
- App: when a game asks for JIT but the debugger is gone, a toast says "JIT is off for this session: StikDebug is no longer attached" and the session runs the interpreter instead of crashing. One new string in every language file.
- Bonus fix for a second definite crash I hit while tracing: changing a GameCube or Wii game's platform ran a Realm write inside another write, which throws an uncatchable exception. Writes now join an open transaction.

**Caveats.** No Xcode on the Pi, so this is unbuilt; the CI workflow compiles it. The iPad runs the `build/ac-events` branch, not main, so the fix needs a merge there after the PR lands. I armed two follow-ups for that moment: merge main into `build/ac-events`, then pull and sign the build onto the iPad.

**Also new.** The Pi can now fetch crash reports and Manic's session logs straight off the iPad over the signer's tunnel. The tool is `~/.local/share/ios-signer/bin/rpcheck-logs` with its source kept beside the signer; it should eventually fold into the better-games signer repo. The signer's existing tool is untouched.
